b.x: Without a license and without the rule of that river, there is no fishing. This page does not teach explosive, poison, a net, or a trap. A hook in the eye is care. A good spot does not get posted.
Before the line gets wet

Gray fishing is a beginner's day, legal and without an audience. You do not go to be seen. You go to learn one gesture and, if the law and the fish allow, to take real food. In Brazil amateur fishing asks for a license. The closed season, the minimum size, and the quota change by river and by species. Confirm the rule of that water before you leave. A reserve, a bridge, a dam, and someone else's land have their own rule. No license, no season, no quota: the rod stays in the car. An amateur license does not allow you to sell the fish.
The kit that fits a common bag

One simple bank rod, between one meter eighty and two meters ten. A small spinning reel. Line from zero point thirty to zero point thirty-five millimeters: thick enough to forgive the first day's mistake. Six hooks, from size two to size eight. Three floats. Small sinkers. Two swivels. Needle-nose pliers. A towel. A cap, water, sunscreen. The license in plastic. A small knife to cut line, not to show. Do not take the box of forty lures on the first day. What does not fit a common bag is not for a beginner. And it is not gray.
Where to stand

A firm bank, water where you can see the bottom or where a local already fishes by day. Do not step into the current to reach the middle. Do not fish under a high-voltage line: the carbon of the rod conducts. Do not take the place of someone already there. Stay a rod's length away, greet them, and be quiet. Sewage, a mine, and water that smells wrong are not a fishing spot: the fish from there is not food. Look at the way out before you rig the rod. If the rain closes in or the river rises, you already know how you return. The gray man does not post the spot. A good hole dies in the first video.
One day's rig

Learn one rig, not five. With a float: the line goes through the float, a small sinker below, the hook at the end. The float marks the depth. If it lies down or sinks with no wind, there is a fish or there is the bottom. On the bottom: the sinker goes at the end, and the hook sits a hand above it, on a short leader. One rod, one line, one hook in the water. A second rod tangles, snags, and calls attention. The gray man fishes with the one in his hand.
Bait the house understands

A worm, cooked corn, or bread dough, where the fish of that place eats it and the rule allows it. Live bait has a rule: some places forbid it. Do not use what you cannot name. One simple lure waits for the second month, when the cast already lands in the same spot. Keep the bait closed. The smell on the hand is normal. The smell in the car seat, all day, is not. Wash the hand before you eat.
The short cast

The first cast is short. Ten meters already teach. Look behind you first: people, a wire, a branch. The float lands, the line tightens without going too slack, and you wait. When the float sinks, count one beat and lift the rod. Do not rip the fish onto the rock. Bring it in slowly, with the rod tip high, and use the reel. The reel's drag stays loose enough for the line to give before it breaks. A small fish you will not eat goes back at once, with a wet hand. A fish under the minimum size always goes back. A forbidden species always goes back, even a large one.
A knot that holds

Pass the end of the line through the eye of the hook twice. Wrap that end five times around the line that goes up to the rod. Pass the end back through the loop that sits next to the eye. Wet the knot with saliva or with the river water. Pull slowly until it seats. Cut the excess and leave a finger of spare line. If it slips, undo it and tie it again. A knot that was not wetted burns the line and opens on the first fish.
The fish and the hook

Hold the fish with a wet hand, firm, without crushing the belly. The pliers take the hook from the mouth if the barb is still visible. If the barb is deep and you will release the fish, cut the line short and let it go: the hook rusts and leaves better than a tear. A hook set in your hand, with the barb inside, does not get pulled. Cut the line, cover it, and get care. A hook in the eye does not get touched. That is care, not fishing. Do not leave the fish suffocating in a bucket all day. Either it goes back to the water in seconds, or it becomes food at once.
Clean and eat

If the rule of the place asks, do not throw the guts in the water. Clean away from the bank, bury them, or take them in a bag. Scale, open the belly, take out what is inside, wash. Ice if the way back is long. Cook until the center is no longer raw. A fish from dirty water, from a city without treatment, or from a fuel smell does not go in the pot. Someone with a fish allergy does not test that at the river. What is left does not stay in the sun. Eat it the same day or bring it back cold to the fridge at home.
What drops the beginner

A wet rock, a bank that gives way, and the wish to take one more step. Do not enter water you have not measured. A boot or a shoe that grips. Do not fish alone, the first time, in a place where no one sees you. Tell someone the hour you return. Thunder: the rod comes down and you leave the open. Sun on the neck drops a person as surely as the river. A child does not stand between the rod and the cast. The hook comes back. The gray man looks before he casts.
What this page refuses

It does not teach explosive, poison, electricity, a gill net, or a trap. It does not teach fishing in the closed season. It does not teach entering forbidden land. It does not teach selling the fish from a weekend license. It does not teach filming the catch or marking the spot on the internet map. Gray fishing is one person, one rod, the rule of that water, and the return before dark.
The first afternoon

Two hours are enough. Check the license. Choose a place by day, with people nearby and a clear way out. Rig the float at home, once, before. Take one bait. Cast short. If no fish comes, the day did not fail: you came back, the line did not break, and you know how to rig it again. The beginner's trophy is not the fish. It is the next Tuesday, on the same river, with the same rod, without an audience.
Read the water

The fish is not in the middle of the mirror. It is where the current delivers food and where it is not seen. Look for the seam: the line between fast water and slow water. Look for the shade of a tree, the rock that breaks the current, the fallen branch that still has a leaf. A deep bank, on one side only, is worth more than a shallow center. You watch for two minutes before you cast. The place that shines and has no edge is almost never the place.
The wait

A still float for minutes is the technique. Moving the bait every twenty seconds scares off what had arrived. Rest the rod. Watch the float, not the phone. A small shiver is wind or it is a mouth. You only act when the float lies down, runs sideways, or disappears. Until then, the hand stays still. Gray fishing is more waiting than casting.
Find the depth

The same float, a hand's width at a time. Start shallow, a hand above the hook. If nothing touches in ten minutes, lower the float one hand. Again. When the float lies down with no fish, you passed the bottom: raise it half a hand. The fish feeds in a band, not in the whole column. Note it in your head: at this spot, two hands down. At the next, start again. Do not guess the depth of the whole river from one point.
The instant of the touch

It sank: count one beat, and lift the tip. Too early, the bait leaves the mouth. Too late, the fish lets go or swallows. The one beat is the span of a short breath, not of a conversation. Lift firm, not a movie yank. If no weight comes, the bait goes back to the same point. Do not sweep the river to hide the mistake.
Bring it in without breaking

Rod tip high. The reel's drag loose enough for the line to give when the fish runs. You do not hoist. You tire it. If it pulls, let a little out and reel again when the pull eases. Do not grab the line with your hand. Do not run backward on the bank. When it reaches the rock, it is already on its side, tired. Then the wet hand. If the line is about to part, it is worth more to let go than to pull until it snaps and leave a hook in the fish for nothing.
Change the spot

Twenty minutes with no touch, and the depth already tested: walk ten steps. Do not sweep the whole bank in five minutes. The fish hears the step on the rock and the talk. Step slowly. The new spot asks for the same two minutes of looking before the cast. Three spots in an afternoon are enough. The fourth is already hurry. If a local is in the best corner, the corner is not yours.
The hour and the light

The start of the day and the end of the day, on the bank, with the way out already seen. The middle of a hard sun is an hour of little feeding and of many mistakes. Night only where the rule of that water allows, and never the first time: the rock that is a path by day is a fall by night. A light, if you need one, stays low, in the hand, for the foot. Do not sweep the sky. Do not light the house on the other side. Thunder ends the fishing at once. A carbon rod in the open, with lightning, is not courage.
Cast under the branch

The overhead swing catches in the tree and delivers the hook to your ear. From below: the rod low, to the side, a short pendulum, the float lands in the shade. Ten meters well placed are worth more than thirty in the middle of nothing. If the branch is over your head, change spots. The fish under the tree is not worth it if the hook comes back into the eye.
The gray man on the bank

A low voice. Trash comes back with you, including the cut line: line on the bank kills birds. Do not show the fish. Do not tell the size to whoever walked by. Do not mark the spot on the phone to publish. If someone asks whether it is good, the answer is short: it is calm. The technique that closes the day is this one. You learned to read, to wait, and to return. The river stays in place for next Tuesday.
